summary: The XRD analysis compares CsPbBr3 quantum dots kept in the dark (S2) with those subjected to light irradiation (S5). Light exposure leads to sharper XRD peaks and the appearance of an additional diffraction peak, suggesting increased crystallinity and possible structural changes. However, quantitative details such as FWHM and phase identification are missing, limiting the depth of interpretation.

key_findings.finding: XRD peaks become sharper after light irradiation, indicating a change in crystallinity.
An additional XRD peak appears at 16.2° after light irradiation.

scientific_interpretation.claim: Light irradiation induces increased crystallinity or grain growth in CsPbBr3 quantum dots, as evidenced by the narrowing of XRD peaks.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The transition from broad to narrow peaks after light exposure suggests larger or more ordered crystalline domains.

citations.evidence: peaks become sharper after light irradiation

scientific_interpretation.claim: The appearance of a new XRD peak at 16.2° after light irradiation suggests a possible structural transformation or the formation of a new crystalline phase/component.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The new peak at 16.2° is not present in the dark-stored sample, indicating a structural change upon illumination.

citations.evidence: additional peak appears near 16.2° after light irradiation

limitations.claim: No quantitative FWHM values are provided, limiting the ability to precisely assess crystallite size or strain.
No explicit phase identification or lattice parameter refinement is reported, so the nature of the new peak at 16.2° cannot be conclusively determined.
The analysis is limited to a single figure and two samples, restricting the generalizability of the observed trends.

citations.evidence: XRD patterns of sample S2 (kept in dark, a) and S5 (after light irradiation, b)
